title: Microservice Premium
summary: Martin Fowler (2015): microservices carry a premium of distributed-system complexity, so most systems should be monoliths; continuous delivery and modularity do not require services.

assertions.quote: microservices introduce complexity on their own account. This adds a premium to a project's cost and risk
The majority of software systems should be built as a single monolithic application.
there's no reason why you can't make a single monolith with well defined module boundaries
there are plenty of organizations that succeed with a cookie-cutter deployment approach: Facebook and Etsy are two well-known examples

verdicts.note: Facebook, Etsy, Shopify and GitHub have all deployed monoliths many times a day.

What DORA finds predictive of continuous delivery is the ability to test and deploy independently; microservices are named only as one architecture that is supposed to enable this, and a footnote warns against decomposing new systems into services prematurely.

assertions.quote: we've seen teams be too eager to embrace microservices

verdicts.note: Microservice envy is widely reported; its magnitude is unmeasured.
